text:
Tessa: getting pings from monitoring: sudden mTLS unwrap failures across eu and apac starting ~04:05 UTC. errors point to KMS Decrypt AccessDenied during cert key unwrap.
Raj: saw that too. sample prod log: `2026-08-10T04:05:12Z proxy-eu unwrap: KMS:AccessDeniedException: Decrypt denied for arn:aws:sts::123456:assumed-role/proxy-keystore`
Marta: I merged a KMS key policy change last night to tighten scope using aws:SourceVpc and an encryption context check. Intended for helper roles only, but pipeline applied it to the shared key resource.
Ben: Oof. If the shared key got that condition, any cross-region fallback decrypts (eu -> us-east) which egress from a different VPC will fail.
oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-4823 created and assigned to eng-security.
Tessa: Can we do a fast revert? Options: (1) revert the key policy (fast), (2) enable operator keystore cache fallback for 5m (risky), (3) route proxies to a regional key (slow). Thoughts?
Raj: revert + temporary 2-5m cache seems reasonable. We removed cache-on-deny a while back to avoid silent misuse, but short operator-led window with alerts is OK.
Marta: I'm reverting now. Change id r-4823-1, rolling via iam pipeline. Posting when applied.
Ben: While Marta reverts, we should improve auditability: add EncryptionContext tags like `service`, `route`, `request_id` to every KMS Decrypt call so CloudTrail ties denies to app requests. Also emit a `kms.decrypt.request_context` log line from the proxy.
Tessa: Good call. Also add a runbook quick query so oncall can find denies fast. Suggest CloudWatch Logs Insights snippet: 
```
fields @timestamp, eventName, awsRegion, userIdentity.arn, requestParameters
| filter eventName = "Decrypt" and errorMessage like /AccessDenied/
| parse requestParameters as params
| sort @timestamp desc
| limit 100
```
Raj: Can we also add a metric from IAM pipeline: `iam.kms.policy.rollout{change_id="...", author="..."}` emitted on successful apply? Should help correlate denies with policy rollouts.
Marta: Revert applied at 04:07:22 UTC, id r-4823-1. Post-deploy checks show decrypt success rate increasing.
Tessa: Confirming TLS handshakes recovering in eu and apac. Monitoring for 45m.
Ben: Follow-ups I'm putting on my radar: (a) implement EncryptionContext propagation and CloudTrail-friendly requestParameters, (b) add a deploy-time policy emulator in the IAM pipeline that simulates Decrypt for a matrix of assumed-role ARNs + known egress VPCs, (c) add a short operator-only keystore cache flag guarded by feature flag + alerting.
Raj: Also add a CI lint rule that flags any KMS key policy changes containing SourceIp or SourceVpc without an explicit allowlist review. And include a smoke decrypt step that runs from each region's NAT egress after a policy deploy.
Marta: Agree. I'll add an infra preflight: emulate policy changes against a curated set of role ARNs and egress paths using the policy simulator API. If any simulated Deny appears for `proxy-keystore` or other critical roles, block rollout.
Tessa: Runbook edits: step 1 is now "check iam.kms.policy.rollout and CloudTrail Decrypt denies"; step 2 includes running the Logs Insights snippet; step 3 check `keystore_cache_fallback` metric and recent policy change ids.
Ben: Also let's add an alert that pages ENGSEC when `kms.decrypt.denies > 5 in 1m` AND `proxy.tls.handshake.failures > 25 in 1m`. Correlation is key.
Raj: Post-incident tasks: ENGSEC-4750 (postmortem + policy audit), INFRA-3321 (policy emulator + smoke decrypt), TOOLING-1247 (CI lint for KMS policy conditions), INFRA-3322 (keystore cache operator flag), SRE-2110 (deploy metric emission).
Marta: Sorry team, the intention was to harden keys. Will add the preflight matrix and notify eng-security before applying similar changes.
Tessa: Quick suggestion: emit a `policy_change_event{resource="key/...", change_id="..."}` to our metrics pipeline so SRE/SEC can graph changes by time.
Ben: I'll add that to the rollout pipeline along with `iam.kms.policy.rollout` metric.
Tessa: Closing loop: monitor for 60m then schedule postmortem. Thanks for the rapid revert and remediation. :thumbsup:
